transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-10-20 16:00 UTC | Duration: 45 mins | Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Jon (Redwood SE), Lena (Greenridge CISO), Mark (Infra), Priya (Legal), Diego (ML Platform)

[00:00] Maya Patel (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call then jump into security posture and hosting options — hosted, dedicated, private.
[00:10] Lena Ortiz (CISO): Hi all. Main concerns: KMS integrations, immutable audit trail, retention and e-discovery controls. We need to validate those before pilot.
[00:22] Jon Ruiz (SE): I'll map the technical answers. Also we'll surface perf implications when we talk private deployments.
[00:30] Mark Chen (Infra): Our constraint: PII and IP must not leave our VPC in cleartext. Hosted looks easiest but may not meet BYOK and retention requirements.
[00:40] Lena: SOC2 type and scope? Any ISO artifacts?
[00:45] Maya: We're SOC2 Type II (Q2 2026). I'll share the report and SSP. We can also provide an ISO alignment summary.
[00:55] Priya Rao (Legal): When you send docs, can that be gated and audited? Access logs required.
[00:59] Maya: Yes — secure link with access logging or SSO-gated retrieval.
[01:05] Diego Alvarez (ML Platform): Technical asks: 1) BYOK for model encryption and disk-at-rest? 2) Audit logs export and retention controls? 3) RBAC scoping for deploys and token minting?
[01:18] Jon: Dedicated supports customer-managed KMS (AWS KMS/HSM) via cross-account roles; Private gives you full key control. Hosted offers managed keys and BYOK in select regions.
[01:30] Mark: Cross-account KMS — what network/IAM setup is required?
[01:33] Jon: Typically IAM roles and key policies; we provide example Terraform snippets. Network-wise, outbound TLS only; we list IP ranges for dedicated pools.
[01:44] Lena: Audit logs need to be immutable for admin actions and crypto ops; retention 1-3 years; WORM preferred.
[01:52] Jon: We stream audit events to customer S3 or SIEM. On Dedicated/Private you control storage and can enable immutability/WORM depending on storage backend; hosted has 12-month default, extendable as an add-on.
[02:06] Priya: Can retention be paused for legal hold and exportable for eDiscovery?
[02:11] Maya: Yes, enterprise features include retention hold workflows and exportable audit bundles.
[02:17] Diego: RBAC needs: deployer, operator, billing reviewer, model auditor. Can policies bind to routes and tokens?
[02:24] Jon: RBAC is role-scoped to projects, models and API routes. Tokens can be minted with TTLs and role bindings.
[02:33] Mark: For private/offline clusters, how are updates and model downloads handled?
[02:38] Jon: For on-prem private we provide offline installers and signed artifact bundles; VPC deployments use mutual-TLS pulls from our registry.
[02:48] Lena: Model weight encryption — disk-level and model checkpoint encryption with customer keys?
[02:53] Jon: Yes, disk encryption with CMKs is standard for Dedicated/Private. We support encrypting checkpoints before load with KMS keys — adds small startup latency.
[03:06] Maya: Is model-level encryption required or preferred for you?
[03:09] Lena: Preferred and likely required for PII in prod. Also need TLS 1.3 and mTLS internally.
[03:18] Jon: TLS 1.3 default; mTLS supported between nodes for private deployments.
[03:25] Priya: Data residency — we have EU/NA separation. Can routing be pinned by region so EU data never leaves EU?
[03:33] Maya: Yes, routing policies can pin to region and failover only to compliant variants; we'll share routing docs.
[03:41] Diego: For POC, we want BYOK, telemetry disabled, logs streamed to our SIEM, and RBAC limited to infra engineers.
[03:48] Jon: That POC config is doable. We'll propose a 1-2 week dedicated POC with those constraints.
[03:55] Mark: KV cache persistence — can it be checkpointed for warm starts?
[03:59] Jon: Default KV cache is in-memory for latency; optional checkpointing to encrypted storage is available for warm starts.
[04:08] Lena: How often do you rotate platform certs and keys? Notifications for compromise?
[04:13] Jon: Customer keys you manage; platform-managed keys rotate annually with emergency rotation procedures. Alerts via security contacts and webhooks.
[04:22] Priya: Export format for logs for chain-of-custody? Signed events?
[04:27] Jon: We export NDJSON with signed hashes and a manifest for chain-of-custody. Sample attached in follow-up.
[04:36] Maya: Cost note: longer retention and audit exports increase storage charges; we'll show pricing scenarios.
[04:43] Mark: Fine as long as unit economics are transparent.
[04:47] Diego: Also want the option to bring our own models into the runtime.
[04:50] Jon: Private and Dedicated support customer models. Hosted requires a vetting step and containerization constraints.
[04:58] Lena: Any third-party pentests and bug bounty info?
[05:02] Maya: Annual third-party pentests and a public bug bounty for critical tiers; summary and timeline forthcoming.
[05:09] Priya: Legal will request indemnity clauses and minimum insurance coverage.
[05:13] Maya: Understood; legal teams will align.
[05:17] Jon: Ops question — split-control for Dedicated? Who owns host accounts?
[05:21] Jon: We offer split-control: customer admin accounts or Redwood-managed hosts with role separation.
[05:28] Maya: Time check. Quick recap and next steps?
[05:31] Lena: Send SOC2, DPA, subprocessor list, Terraform/VPC diagram and a POC plan with pricing for a 2-week dedicated POC.
[05:39] Maya: Confirmed. Action items: Maya to send security bundle by 2026-10-22; Jon to share VPC snippets by 2026-10-23; Diego to provide workload samples by 2026-10-25.
[05:52] Diego: Will prepare sample prompt sets and token distribution.
[05:56] Priya: We'll review DPA and return markups.
[06:01] Maya: We'll follow up with POC kickoff invite once scope is agreed. Thanks everyone.
[06:05] All: Thanks, bye.

Notes: Automated transcript had a few mis-hears ("K-V cash" for KV cache), occasional speaker label swaps. Shared artifacts referenced: SOC2 report, System Security Plan, DPA, VPC Terraform snippets, private deploy diagram, sample NDJSON log export.

End of transcript.
